instructions.question: What overall sentiment does the tweet's author express or convey about its topic: positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Positive needs explicit enthusiasm, praise, interest or celebration; an achievement, win, or new product feature or launch; or an outing framed as a treat, shared with a loved one or eagerly wanted. Negative covers complaints, disappointment, anger, mockery, personal mishaps, mixed reviews ending in a complaint, and reports of violence, injuries or criminal charges. Neutral covers ads, bare check-ins, flat or indifferent plans, plain news, critique of play or politics without insults, questions, balanced views and trivial joking gripes.

neutral.what: Ads, listings, bare check-ins, flat plans; news with no harm or achievement; analytical opinions; balanced views; joking gripes about trivial matters.
examples: Make sure you buy tickets for Mobtown Moon Preview at Creative Alliance on Sat, Sep 8 !
Goin to the Ed Sheeran concert Thursday and I haven't really listened to him lol #whatislife
Fake punt on 4th and 11? Wow, James Franklin can make some odd decisions. #PennState #Michigan #PSUvsMICH
neutral.cues: don't miss, get ready, register, I'm going to, who wants to, may, reportedly, scores
neutral.not_for: Violence, injuries or charges (negative); achievements or explicit delight (positive).

positive.what: Excitement, praise, love, interest or celebration; achievements, wins; new tech or product features; outings the author clearly wants or shares with someone special.
examples: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!
Surprising my mom with AC/DC tickets for Wednesday. Just going to show up
I just saw a glance at the new Galaxy Note 5. Looks interesting. That may be my next phone.
positive.cues: can't wait, love, excited, great, interesting, good experience, should be fun, I really want to, 1st place, now works with, new, !!
positive.not_for: Venue ads, 'I'm going to X - date' check-ins, indifferent plans (neutral); sarcastic praise (negative).

negative.what: Sadness, anger, frustration, disappointment, insults, mockery, mishaps, reviews ending in a complaint, and reports of violence, injuries or charges.
examples: still so sad I'm not going to Ed Sheeran the 25th :////
I saw Paper Towns on Friday, it was good I guess but there was so much changes compares to the book, it bothered me
RT @user Gavin Henson looks set to miss the Rugby World Cup after dislocating a bone in his right wrist yesterday
negative.cues: sad, bored, tedious, stuck, hate, worst, pathetic, bothered me, wtf, :/, :(, attack, injured, charged
negative.not_for: Calm analysis of a team or politician, joking gripes about one's evening (neutral).
